remaining_gaps.rule: A once-this-turn Repeat permission can be spent on a card that entered play after the permission was granted.
remaining_gaps.candidate_question: Spirit A uses Powerstorm on Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares. Afterwards Bringer uses Call on Midnight’s Dream in a legal land with Dahan, gains a Fast Major Power, Forgets Call on Midnight’s Dream for the Major gain, and uses its conditional permission to play the new Major immediately. Bringer then uses that new Major normally. Assume sufficient Energy, valid targets, and no other restrictions. May Bringer spend the previously granted Powerstorm Repeat on this new Major even though it was not in play when Powerstorm resolved?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: Yes. Powerstorm grants the Spirit a general once-this-turn Repeat option, not a permission restricted to cards already in play at grant time. The new Major is eligible once it is in play; Bringer can pay its cost and Repeat it at its current Speed. Forgetting Call on Midnight’s Dream does not remove the separate new Major.
remaining_gaps.core_applicability: Original Powerstorm and Call on Midnight’s Dream printed faces have no expansion mark. Call on Midnight’s Dream explicitly supplies the later Major gain/play; no expansion producer is imported. The named Major may be any original-core Fast Major meeting the stated assumptions.
remaining_gaps.why_existing_actual_prompts_do_not_reque: Q40 asks whether the Repeat card must be chosen immediately, whether it can be Slow/an Innate, and whether printed Elements recur. A respondent may correctly allow later choice among the grant-time cards while wrongly excluding cards played afterwards. Q37/Q38 ask gaining and extra-play timing, with no Repeat eligibility question. Q88 asks the opposite departure branch: the Forgotten original card cannot later be Repeated. Q41/Q42/Q43/Q95/Q106/Q107/Q111/Q114 concern modifiers, chaining, destination, Speed, counts, use limits, or retargeting; none asks whether a later entrant can receive an earlier Repeat permission.
remaining_gaps.novelty_reason: The FAQ expressly defines the grant-to-use temporal eligibility boundary. This is an independently published permission, beyond combining extra-play arithmetic with deferred selection. The scenario demonstrates that permission without inventing a new rule.

remaining_gaps.rule: Standard core has no per-land stacking cap for any piece.
remaining_gaps.candidate_question: In a standard core game a land is already crowded with Invaders, Dahan, and Spirit Presence. Can a general per-land stacking limit prevent an otherwise legal Build, Gather, or Presence placement there? Do any of those three types of piece have such a default cap?
remaining_gaps.predetermined_answer: No. There is no default stacking limit for any piece, so crowding alone cannot prevent those otherwise legal additions or movements. Each specific action must still obey its normal instructions. A large Presence stack still forms only one Sacred Site for that Spirit in that land.
remaining_gaps.core_applicability: The ruling explicitly describes the default game and names Adversary/Scenario caps as exceptions. Those excluded exceptions are not invoked. CORE p.13 independently permits any number of Presence in a land.
remaining_gaps.why_existing_actual_prompts_do_not_reque: Q23 asks mixed-Spirit Sacred Site ownership, whether four Presence create two sites, and the meaning of your land. It establishes the site-counting outcome for that particular stack, without asking a default land-cap rule. Q22 asks whether setup placements may share a land. Q33 asks whether Dahan/Invaders are limited by the physical supply, which is a global component-availability rule and leaves a distinct per-land-cap misconception untested. The other movement/build questions never request whether existing crowding prohibits an otherwise legal action.
remaining_gaps.novelty_reason: This is an explicit spatial-capacity permission for all piece types, distinct from inventory availability and Sacred Site counting. The candidate uses no numerical variants and tests one general rule.

No material answer contradiction, required correction, scope error, or unresolved material ambiguity was found. Preserve all fixed entries.
fixed_key_audit.scope_handling: Original 2017 balanced standard core and applicable linked official corrections only. Named expansion symbols, rather than catalog labels, controlled card membership. Broad FAQ material about Adversaries, Scenarios, thematic maps, optional difficulty, expansions, promos, and publishing was read but excluded from coverage requirements. Explicit hypothetical repeated Ravages, simultaneous Blight, and changed Speed were evaluated as given rather than importing an excluded producer.

stopping_assessment: The two documented zero-addition passes 20/21 do not establish saturation: the precise future-card eligibility clause and the general per-land capacity clause remain unrequested by the actual 125 prompts. Their broad map categories and surplus key wording cannot supply that missing coverage. Reopen the stopping claim for adjudication of G01/G02; this review makes no edits to frozen entries.

novelty_notes.reason: Replacement retaining Damage and immediate destruction when reduced/new Health is met are already requested by Q18. Keep the fixed entry, without extra coverage credit.
Illegal human cleanup, destination, and non-movement classification already appear in Q80/Q81. Keep the fixed entry, without extra coverage credit.

Q21 directly asks geometric self-adjacency and within-Range-1 distance. Q125 additionally asks how a printed Power Range number constrains legal targets: the printed value is a maximum rather than an exact distance. Knowing that a land is geometrically within Range 1 does not itself establish that a card printed Range 1 allows it. CORE p.16 explicitly states the printed-range permission. Credit that single extra interpretation rule; do not count the repeated self-distance fact a second time.
Q17 requests the complete ordinary Gain procedure. Its same-bullet reshuffle instruction is part of that directly requested procedure; changing deck counts supplies no distinct rule.
